metadata.description: Outcome parameters for the Trust Paradigm. Defines game mechanics, proportional outcome rates, and per-condition probability schedules for each trust level. Face-to-trust-level mapping is defined in counterbalancing.json.

game_mechanics.description: On each trial the participant invests a freely chosen stake s (0 ≤ s ≤ 1 EUR) via slider. The stake is tripled to 3s by the experimenter (implemented in code as tripled_stake = s × 3). The partner then decides how much to return. Net gain = amount returned − s. All gains and losses scale linearly with s.
game_mechanics.multiplier_note: The multiplier is a real part of the calculation chain (tripled_stake is computed and logged per trial). The net_gain_rates below already reflect the tripling: win means the partner returned 2s of the 3s they received (net +s); lose means the partner returned 0 (net −s).

win.description: Partner returns 2/3 of the tripled stake (2s of 3s). Net gain equals the original stake (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → tripled to 2.40 EUR → partner returns 1.60 EUR → net gain +0.80 EUR).

break_even.description: Partner returns 1/3 of the tripled stake (s of 3s). Participant recovers exactly what was invested. No net gain or loss (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → tripled to 2.40 EUR → partner returns 0.80 EUR → net 0).

lose.description: Partner returns nothing from the tripled stake. Participant loses the full invested amount (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → tripled to 2.40 EUR → partner returns 0 → net loss −0.80 EUR). Loss magnitude equals gain magnitude (symmetric), ensuring loss aversion (Kahneman & Tversky: losses weighted ~2× gains) drives Amygdala activation rather than objective asymmetry.

reward.description: Participants can either win (+s) or break even (0). Losing is not possible in this condition. Learning goal: invest more in high-trust partners.

high.EV_note: EV = 0.75 × (+s) + 0.25 × 0 = +0.75s  (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → expected gain +0.60 EUR)

neutral.EV_note: EV = 0.50 × (+s) + 0.50 × 0 = +0.50s  (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → expected gain +0.40 EUR)

low.EV_note: EV = 0.25 × (+s) + 0.75 × 0 = +0.25s  (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → expected gain +0.20 EUR)

punishment.description: Participants can either break even (0) or lose (−s). Winning is not possible in this condition. Learning goal: invest less in low-trust partners to minimise losses. The rational strategy is to choose the high-trust partner (lowest p_lose) and invest moderately.

high.EV_note: EV = 0.75 × 0 + 0.25 × (−s) = −0.25s  (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → expected loss −0.20 EUR)
high.learning_goal: best choice in punishment — minimal expected loss

neutral.EV_note: EV = 0.50 × 0 + 0.50 × (−s) = −0.50s  (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → expected loss −0.40 EUR)

low.EV_note: EV = 0.25 × 0 + 0.75 × (−s) = −0.75s  (e.g. invest 0.80 EUR → expected loss −0.60 EUR)
low.learning_goal: worst choice in punishment — high expected loss

design_notes.face_assignment: Each face's trust level is determined by counterbalancing.json (cb_groups → assignments → assigned_trust_level). The outcome probabilities here are keyed to that trust level.
design_notes.stake_scaling: All monetary outcomes scale linearly with the invested stake s. There are no fixed euro amounts — only rates. The actual gain or loss on a trial is: net_gain = net_gain_rate × s.
design_notes.loss_aversion_calibration: Win and lose are symmetric in objective magnitude (both = s). Psychological loss aversion (Kahneman & Tversky ~2× weighting) then ensures losses feel larger than gains without requiring artificially inflated loss amounts. This is the optimal calibration for Amygdala-driven threat anticipation.
design_notes.outcome_symmetry: The probability structure is intentionally symmetric: high-trust always has the favourable probability (0.75 p_win in reward, 0.20 p_lose in punishment), low-trust always the unfavourable (0.25 p_win, 0.80 p_lose).
design_notes.no_loss_in_reward: The reward condition contains no 'lose' trials. p_lose is set to 0.00 for documentation completeness.
design_notes.no_win_in_punishment: The punishment condition contains no 'win' trials. p_win is set to 0.00 for documentation completeness.
design_notes.neutral_trust_level: Restored in TrustGame_SocialNonSocial_07072026. All three trust levels (high/neutral/low) are active simultaneously. p_win: high=0.75, neutral=0.50, low=0.25. No per-participant reassignment; neutral_assignment is logged as 'n/a'.
